rows.grounds: compound: kula+ācāra+paribhraṣṭa; dual subject fallen from Kula conduct
result for those fallen from conduct

items.question: What hellish destination awaits those fallen from Kula conduct?
premises: Some fall away from Kula conduct.
Raurava is a named hell.
Such fallen ones go to that hell.
items.inference: Those who abandon Kula conduct incur the consequence of going to the Raurava hell.
items.plain_english: Those who have fallen from Kula conduct would go to the Raurava hell.

rows.grounds: compound: kula+bhraṣṭa; person fallen from Kula

items.question: Is any expiation available for one who has fallen from Kula?
premises: A person may fall from Kula.
Expiation would be a remedy for such a fall.
No expiation is seen anywhere for such a person.
items.inference: Falling from Kula is presented as having no available expiation.
items.plain_english: O Lady of Gods, no expiation is ever seen anywhere for one who has fallen from Kula.

rows.grounds: compound: mahā+pātakin; one guilty of great transgression

items.question: How is the fallen Kula practitioner characterized in moral terms?
premises: The fallen one acts according to whim.
Such conduct constitutes grave transgression.
The Goddess is addressed as beloved.
items.inference: The one fallen from Kula is characterized as a willful doer of great sins.
uncertainties: This verse continues the description begun in verse 1314.
items.plain_english: O beloved, he acts as he pleases and is a great sinner.

rows.grounds: group of female powers or deities
prakopa with enclitic ca; wrath of the yoginis
repeated locative expression indicating constant occurrence

items.question: What immediate afflictions befall one who has fallen from Kula conduct?
premises: The yoginis can become wrathful.
The fallen one experiences stumbles.
These stumbles occur at every step.
items.inference: The fallen practitioner suffers the anger of the yoginis and repeated failures.
items.plain_english: There is the anger of the yoginis, and stumbles at every step.

rows.grounds: compound: deśa+deśāntara; wandering from one region to another
compound: kārya+hāni with enclitic ca; failure of undertakings

items.question: What ongoing worldly hardships afflict the one fallen from Kula?
premises: The fallen one wanders from place to place.
The fallen one suffers loss of undertakings.
These hardships occur continually.
items.inference: Falling from Kula leads to constant instability and failure in worldly affairs.
items.plain_english: He goes from one place to another, and there is always loss of his undertakings.

rows.grounds: the yoginis consume or destroy the fallen
mayā with enclitic eva; emphasizes the giver

items.question: By what divine authorization do the yoginis destroy those fallen from Kula?
premises: The yoginis devour the fallen.
A boon was granted to them formerly.
That boon was given by the speaker alone.
items.inference: The yoginis' destruction of the fallen is sanctioned by a boon granted by the divine speaker.
items.plain_english: They devour him; indeed, formerly a boon was given to them by me alone.

rows.grounds: compound: catur+veda; the four Vedic collections
compound: an+ācāra; those lacking proper conduct

items.question: What harm do those lacking proper conduct cause to sacred tradition?
premises: Some are without proper conduct.
The four Vedas represent sacred tradition.
Those without conduct destroy the four Vedas.
items.inference: Lack of proper conduct is said to undermine even the authority of the four Vedas.
items.plain_english: O Lady of Kula, those without proper conduct destroy the four Vedas.

rows.grounds: compound: tad+viparyaya; from the opposite of proper conduct

items.question: What degraded rebirth results for Kaula practitioners who reverse proper conduct?
premises: Kaula practitioners are subject to consequences.
Reversal of proper conduct is possible.
Such reversal leads to the state of an animal.
items.inference: Kaula practitioners who act contrary to proper conduct attain an animal state.
items.plain_english: By the reversal of that, Kaula practitioners attain the state of animals.

rows.grounds: compound: ājñā+siddhi with future verb; fulfillment of the command

items.question: What spiritual accomplishment follows from the observance of proper conduct?
premises: Proper conduct can be observed.
Observance of conduct has a result.
That result is the accomplishment of the command.
items.inference: Observing proper conduct truly brings about the accomplishment of the command.
uncertainties: The exact scope of ājñāsiddhi is not specified in this verse.
items.plain_english: Truly, from the observance of proper conduct, the accomplishment of the command will come to be.

rows.grounds: compound: kula+dharma; the duty or law of Kula
compound: sat+ācāra; right or proper conduct

items.question: What is identified as the foundational cause of Kula duty?
premises: Kula duty has a cause.
Good conduct is named as that cause.
The Goddess is addressed as Lady of Kula.
items.inference: Good conduct is the foundational cause of Kula duty.
items.plain_english: O Lady of Kula, good conduct is the cause of Kula duty.

rows.grounds: one who keeps the samaya or rule
kaulika with enclitics ca and api; also a Kaula practitioner

items.question: What status belongs to the one who knows and observes the vow?
premises: One may know and be observant of the vow.
Such a person is identified as Kaula.
The Goddess is addressed as Shambhavi.
items.inference: The knower who observes the vow is affirmed to be a Kaula practitioner.
uncertainties: The token cāpi appears again as a separate token in the list; its repetition may be emphatic or textual.
items.plain_english: O Shambhavi, he who knows and observes the vow would be a Kaula practitioner as well.

rows.grounds: compound: deha+pāta; at the time of death
compound: samaya+ācāra+pālana; maintaining conduct according to the vow

items.question: What final liberation results from observing the conduct of the vow?
premises: The fall of the body marks death.
Conduct according to the vow can be observed.
Such observance leads to liberation at death.
items.inference: Observance of vow-conduct results in liberation at the time of death.
items.plain_english: Through the observance of the conduct of the vow, there would be liberation at the fall of the body.
